about: The concerns buyers raise most on a sales call, with what each one usually means and a question-led answer. Plain drafts in the member's voice, filled with their own facts (braces). Seven come up for every business; three more are picked for the kind of business. No statistics or claims about real businesses live here.

price.label: Price
says: That's more than I wanted to spend.
That's too expensive.
Can you do it cheaper?
price.means: They don't yet see why it's worth the price to them, or they're comparing it to the wrong thing.
price.answer: That's fair. Can I ask what you're comparing it to? Most of the price is that {difference}. If the total is the problem, we can start with {smaller} and add the rest later.
price.ask: Is it the price itself, or not being sure it's worth it?
price.avoid: Don't drop your price on the spot. Change what's included, not the price.

think_about_it.label: I need to think about it
says: I need to think about it.
Let me sleep on it.
I'll get back to you.
think_about_it.means: There's a concern they haven't said out loud yet. Usually it's the price, the timing, or whether it will work for them.
think_about_it.answer: Of course. So I know what to send you, what's the part you want to think over? Is it the price, the timing, or whether it'll work for you?
think_about_it.ask: If this were an easy yes, what would have to be true?
think_about_it.avoid: Don't push for a yes today. Find the real concern, answer that one, then offer to hold a date.

timing.label: Not right now
says: Not right now, maybe next month.
Call me after the holidays.
It's not a good time.
timing.means: It isn't a priority yet, or something else is going on. Sometimes it's a polite no.
timing.answer: No problem at all. What's going on between now and then? If it helps, I can pencil you in for {laterDate} and check in with you a few days before.
timing.ask: What would make next month a better time than now?
timing.avoid: Don't just say "okay, talk later." Agree on a date to check back in.

partner.label: I need to ask my partner
says: I need to talk to my husband first.
Let me check with my wife.
I have to ask my partner.
saysBusiness: I need to check with my business partner.
My co-owner has to sign off.
partner.means: They want to share the decision, or they need an easy way to explain the price at home.
partner.answer: Makes sense, it's a shared decision. What do you think they'll ask first? I'll give you the short version so it's easy to explain, and I'm happy to do a quick call with you both.
partner.ask: If it were just up to you, would you go ahead?
partner.avoid: Don't go around them. Help them make the case to their partner.

decision_maker.label: It's not my decision
says: I have to run it by my boss.
The owner decides on this.
It has to go through the office.
decision_maker.means: They may like it but can't say yes. You need to know what the person who decides cares about.
decision_maker.answer: Totally fair. What will they want to know first: the price, the timing, or the result? I'll send a one-page summary you can forward, and I'm glad to join a 10-minute call with them.
decision_maker.ask: Is it your call how this gets done, or theirs?
decision_maker.avoid: Don't send a long deck. Send one page and offer a short call with the person who signs.

time.label: No time for this
says: I don't have time for this right now.
I'm swamped.
I can't take on one more thing.
time.means: They think it will add work to their plate.
time.answer: That's the point of it. From you it takes {effort}, and I handle the rest. {timeSaved}
time.ask: If it took less than 10 minutes of your time, would it be worth doing now?
time.avoid: Don't argue that they have time. Show how little it takes from them.

tried_before.label: Tried it before
says: I tried something like this before and it didn't work.
We had someone do this and it was a mess.
I've been burned before.
tried_before.means: They were let down once and don't want to feel that again.
tried_before.answer: I'm glad you told me. What happened last time? Here's what I do differently: {difference}. {promise}
tried_before.ask: What would need to be different this time?
tried_before.avoid: Don't knock the last person. Ask what went wrong and show how you handle that part.

cheaper.label: Someone's cheaper
says: I found someone cheaper.
I got a lower quote.
Another place quoted me less.
cheaper.means: They're comparing prices without comparing what's included.
cheaper.answer: Good to compare. Can you check what's included in theirs? Mine includes {included}. If you want a lower price, {smaller} is an option.
cheaper.ask: Apart from price, what would make you pick one over the other?
cheaper.avoid: Don't match their price. Compare what's included.

diy.label: I can do it myself
says: I can just do it myself.
My son usually does it.
We'll figure it out ourselves.
diy.means: They're not sure it's worth paying someone for.
diy.answer: You definitely could. The question is whether you want to spend your time on it. {timeSaved} And it's done right the first time.
diy.ask: When did you last get a chance to do it yourself?
diy.avoid: Don't make it sound hard. Make it sound like time they get back.

send_info.label: Send me some info
says: Can you send me some info?
Just email me something.
Do you have a brochure?
send_info.means: Often a polite way out. Sometimes they really do want to read it first.
send_info.answer: Sure. So I send the right thing, what do you want to know most: the price, what's included, or when I could start? I'll send that and check back with you on {day}.
send_info.ask: What would you look for in it to decide?
send_info.avoid: Don't send a brochure and wait. Send one page and set the date you'll follow up.

proof.label: Will it work for me?
says: How do I know it'll work?
Do you have reviews?
Have you done this for someone like me?
proof.means: They want to see it working for someone like them before they pay.
proof.answer: Fair question. Here's what I can show you: {proof}. {promise}
proof.ask: What would you want to see to feel sure?
proof.avoid: Don't make up numbers or reviews. Show real work, even if it was for friends or family.

budget.label: No budget
says: We don't have the budget for this.
Money's tight right now.
It's not in the budget this month.
budget.means: The money isn't set aside yet, or this isn't a priority next to other bills.
budget.answer: Understood. Where does this sit next to the other things you're paying for? {smaller} fits a smaller budget, and you can add the rest later.
budget.ask: If budget weren't the issue, would this be the right fit?
budget.avoid: Don't guess what they can afford. Ask, then offer the smaller start.

already_have.label: We already have someone
says: We already have someone for that.
My cousin does it for us.
We use another company.
already_have.means: They're loyal, or they just haven't looked around in a while.
already_have.answer: Good, that means it matters to you. How happy are you with them, out of 10? If it's not a 10, what would make it one?
already_have.ask: What would they need to do better?
already_have.avoid: Don't criticize the person they use now.

trust.label: Who are you?
says: I've never heard of you.
How long have you been doing this?
Are you insured?
trust.means: They don't know you yet and don't want to take a risk on someone new.
trust.answer: Fair question. I'm newer, which means you get me on every job and I care about each one. {promise}
trust.ask: What would help you feel comfortable trying me?
trust.avoid: Don't stretch the truth about how long you've been doing this. New and careful beats vague.

contract.label: Don't want to be locked in
says: I don't want to be locked into a contract.
What if it doesn't work out?
Is there a commitment?
contract.means: They're worried about being stuck if it isn't a fit.
contract.answer: Makes sense. We can start with {smaller}, and you decide what's next after you see it.
contract.ask: What would you need to see in the first month to keep going?
contract.avoid: Don't hide your terms. Say plainly how to stop.
